correctness.rationale: When the hub is blue, the white induced graph consists of rim path components if and only if >=2 rim vertices are blue; blue boundary rim vertices peel the white paths, while 0 or 1 blue rim vertices leave no first move (for 1, the unique blue rim vertex has two white rim neighbors and the blue hub sees >=3 whites). Without a blue hub, any remaining white rim vertex connects the entire white induced graph through the white universal hub; a blue rim vertex has exactly one white neighbor iff its two cyclic rim neighbors are blue, exactly a run of three blue consecutive rim vertices. Such a middle vertex forces the hub, reducing to the first case. Hub-contained min sets: choose 2 rims; hub-free min sets: exactly m length-three rim runs, so binom(m,2)+m=binom(n,2). Standard 4-state 00,01,10,11 de Bruijn transfer with forbidden 11->11 and 1-transition weight x has tr(T^m) equal the cyclic 111-avoiding polynomial. Independent direct PSD-component forcing on all subsets of W_5..W_12 exactly reproduced structural criterion, across 8,160 possible subsets, with orderwise successful totals 16,37,82,177,372,773,1594,3269; finite checks corroborate proof.
residual_risks: The wheel convention here uses n total vertices, rim length n-1, and n>=5; W_4=K_4 uses different small-case convention.
Positive semidefinite component forcing is distinct from ordinary zero forcing.

final_claim: For wheel W_n with n>=5, a positive semidefinite zero forcing set S contains the hub and at least two rim vertices, or excludes the hub and contains three consecutive rim vertices. Consequently Z+=3 (known), number of minimum sets binom(n,2), and the full forcing-set cardinality enumerator is x((1+x)^m-1-mx)+(1+x)^m-tr(T(x)^m), m=n-1, T transfer matrix forbidding cyclic 111.
limitations: The wheel convention here uses n total vertices, rim length n-1, and n>=5; W_4=K_4 uses different small-case convention.
